item.title: Are We Becoming Feudal Again?
item.description:
Draft for review — all comments welcome

There is a peculiar contradiction in the life of a reasonably well-paid professional. We enjoy a degree of material comfort, security and personal freedom that would have been unimaginable to most people throughout history. We can travel, own property, change occupations and, at least in principle, choose how we wish to live. Yet for many of us, the practical exercise of those freedoms is considerably more difficult than their legal existence might suggest.

item.title: Across the Strait: The Johor–Singapore Growth Story
item.description:
Singapore and Johor are separated by a narrow strait, yet combining their economic strengths is much harder than simply crossing the Causeway.

Updated 29 October 2026; updated again 5 November 2026.

Working draft

This article sets out a hypothesis before primary research. I have published it to invite feedback and discussion. As the evidence develops, so too will the argument.

Across the strait

Stand on the waterfront in Johor Bahru after the evening rain has cleared and the wind comes clean off the water. The high-rises of Singapore emerge across the Johor strait, their lights hard and bright against the dark.
